title: Drop the promise on the cash ISA limit
name: Drop the promise on the cash ISA limit
headline: Drop the cash ISA promise. Raises £0.0bn in 2029-30.
description: The Budget keeps the cash ISA limit at £20,000 from April 2027, rather than cutting it as had been floated. Switch this on to drop that and let the limit fall as the Treasury’s pre-Budget plans had it.

baselinePolicy.text: The cash ISA limit stays at £20,000 from 6 April 2027 (Table 6.1 line 11).

source.quote: Maintain the cash ISA limit at £20,000 from 6 April 2027

alreadyIncludes: The cash ISA limit stays at £20,000 from 6 April 2027 (Table 6.1 line 11).

lines.title: Cash ISAs: Maintain the cash ISA limit at £20,000 from 6 April 2027

rawSource.note: Reversal: the Treasury’s costing with its sign reversed (positive scorecard values reduce borrowing; here receipts positive means more revenue).

caveats: The Treasury’s costing is on the OBR October 2026 forecast, the baseline used here. Effects before the start year are not applied: 2026-27 falls before any Budget of yours.
Small money: the line is the cost of not cutting the limit, so this card raises little.

considerations.text: The Treasury’s scorecard figure is the certified direct costing for the measure, including the behavioural response the Treasury and OBR agreed; the Budget 2026 policy costings document gives the method.
